interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is documented. No lymph nodes were sampled; pNx does not establish node-negative disease and widens uncertainty. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 59.37 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 35.62–83.12 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 8.8. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pT2c stage, positive surgical margins, and lymphovascular invasion, with no seminal vesicle invasion. The absence of documented nodal sampling, resulting in a pNx status, widens the uncertainty regarding local control. The difference between biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted as missing, which impacts the certainty of the pathological assessment.

Countervailing factors include the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The lack of documented postoperative PSA or follow-up data prevents a definitive assessment of the subsequent PSA trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would significantly revise this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 59.37 months without an event. Missing nodal sampling further complicates the certainty of the outcome assessment.

The patient underwent robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c, ISUP grade group 2, and positive surgical margins. Seminal vesicles were not invaded, but lymphovascular invasion was present. A key factor influencing prognosis is the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The status of lymph nodes is uncertain as no nodes were removed, and "no lymph nodes were removed." Preoperative PSA was 8.8. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. The uncertainty in nodal sampling widens the prognostic range. The current prognostic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 59.37 months without an event. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would revise this assessment.
